target_customer: Every online shopper in India, with no specific segment identified.
failure_reasons: Established marketplaces have scale, logistics and brand that a new entrant cannot match on commission alone.
Both buyers and sellers must be won at the same time, and neither has a reason to join an empty marketplace.
Matching delivery speed requires a logistics network that costs far more than the starting budget.

compliance_flags.note: Marketplace operators face consumer-protection and e-commerce rules for sellers, returns and grievance handling. Verify with official sources; this is not legal advice.
Holding seller payouts can trigger payment-aggregator rules. Verify with official sources; this is not legal advice.
Marketplaces have specific GST collection and registration duties. Verify with official sources; this is not legal advice.

market_saturation.justification: Dominant, well-funded marketplaces already serve the same buyers and sellers.

operational_complexity.justification: Logistics, returns, seller onboarding and disputes must all work from day one.

compliance.justification: Marketplace, payments and tax obligations are heavy.

capital_need.justification: Matching delivery speed needs far more capital than savings.

founder_load.justification: One founder cannot run supply, demand, logistics and support.

suggested_pivots: Pick one narrow category and city and serve it better than a general marketplace.
Build a seller tool for existing marketplaces instead of a competing marketplace.
